hypotheses.claim: FRANK's heterogeneous loop-of-loops can be represented in ClayCode as typed loop/coupling/readout state over the existing G9 semantic core, with execution supplied by generic structured control-flow/runtime lowering rather than a FRANK-specific core syntax primitive.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production FRANK/ClayCode program whose recurrent semantics cannot be expressed or safely lowered without adding a new core semantic primitive.

hypotheses.claim: Outcome/pressure-gated adaptive recurrence with explicit convergence, productive-cycle, stall and divergence classes will outperform or reduce cost versus fixed recurrence budgets on frozen FRANK replay episodes without increasing unsafe halts or authority leakage.
evidence: local proxy demonstrates representability and class separation only
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched H1/H2 replay shows no verified task/cost/recovery benefit or unacceptable false halt/rollback behavior.

hypotheses.claim: A new FRANK-specific ClayCode core loop syntax/semantic primitive is necessary to represent the loop-of-loops architecture.
evidence: candidate parsed and executed via existing typed IR/runtime forms without such a primitive
hypotheses.scope_limit: Does not prove production compiler completeness.

hypotheses.claim: Every healthy FRANK recurrent process should converge to a fixed point.
evidence: bounded 2D period-4 orbit retained positive utility and was correctly classified PRODUCTIVE_LIMIT_CYCLE
hypotheses.scope_limit: The counterexample establishes that fixed-point convergence cannot be a universal health criterion; it does not prove any specific live FRANK cycle is useful.
